record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.original_question: Can the same fixed-point iteration method be used to construct new flat steady states of the Vlasov-Poisson system, especially steady states relevant as Newtonian disk-galaxy models, where existing results are limited?

evidence.quote: We have not only in mind the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system but also in the case of the Vlasov-Poisson system there is hope that this method can be used to construct new solutions, namely flat steady states. Presently there are only limited results in the literature about such solutions, cf. [35], and they are of interest as models of disk galaxies, cf. [18].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Vlasov–Poisson system in three spatial dimensions modeling a self-gravitating collisionless gas. Let f = f(t,x,v) ≥ 0 denote the phase-space density on R^3 × R^3, satisfying

  ∂_t f + v · ∇_x f − ∇_x U · ∇_v f = 0,
  ΔU = 4π ρ,  ρ(t,x) = ∫_{R^3} f(t,x,v) dv,  U(t,x) → 0 as |x| → ∞.

A "flat" steady state is a time-independent solution f = f_0(x,v) whose spatial support is concentrated on a two-dimensional disk {x_3 = 0} ⊂ R^3, with a corresponding axially symmetric induced potential U; such configurations serve as Newtonian models of disk galaxies. A general framework for producing steady states is the following fixed-point iteration: given an ansatz f = φ(E, L) where E = |v|^2/2 + U(x) is the particle energy and L is the angular momentum about the symmetry axis, define the operator T that sends a candidate potential U to the potential U' generated (via the Poisson equation) by the spatial density associated with φ(E_U, L); a steady state corresponds to a fixed point U = T(U).

Problem. Develop a rigorous fixed-point iteration scheme of this type that produces flat (disk-supported) axially symmetric steady states of the Vlasov–Poisson system. In particular, identify a function space and a class of microscopic ansatz functions φ for which T admits a fixed point yielding genuine flat steady states, including configurations relevant as Newtonian disk-galaxy models (e.g., those exhibiting flat rotation curves).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024) establishes a mass-preserving fixed-point algorithm and proves existence of fixed points in the spherically symmetric Vlasov–Poisson case, with the authors stating belief that the result extends to the flat axially symmetric case but without a full proof yet. Numerical construction of flat steady states with flat rotation curves has been carried out, while a complete rigorous existence theorem covering the disk-galaxy-relevant flat solutions via the fixed-point method remains open. Some related variational (Energy-Casimir) existence and stability results for flat Vlasov–Poisson steady states exist but do not cover the same class.

status_evidence.title: Steady states of the spherically symmetric Vlasov-Poisson system as fixed points of a mass-preserving algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: A mass-preserving algorithm... formulated as a fixed point problem, existence proven in spherically symmetric case; authors believe extension to flat axially symmetric case is possible.
status_evidence.claim: Fixed-point method established in spherical case; flat axially symmetric extension stated as conjectural/future work, indicating the flat case is not yet rigorously resolved.

status_evidence.title: Existence and stability of steady states of Flat Vlasov Poisson with a central mass density
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of steady states of the Flat Vlasov-Poisson system via Energy-Casimir minimization with external potential.
status_evidence.claim: Partial existence results for flat steady states exist via variational methods, but do not implement the fixed-point iteration approach for general disk-galaxy models.
